media_decisions.audio: Skipped. The Himalayan Database is a structured numeric archive about climbing expeditions; sound is not part of the dataset and a generated soundscape would be decorative rather than explanatory. The story is carried by charts, photographs of the mountain environment, and prose.
media_decisions.video: Skipped. Two production hero images carry the visual atmosphere; running text2video for ambient mountain footage would not add information beyond what static images already convey, and would slow the page.
media_decisions.map: Skipped as a dedicated section. The data has only seven REGION_FACTOR groups and the marquee peaks are clustered in two regions (Khumbu and Annapurna-Manaslu); a chart that lists peaks by region carries the same information more legibly than a tiny choropleth of Nepal.
media_decisions.instances: No instance embeds. The dataset is statistical, not media-anchored - there is no song, painting, or specimen photo to embed.

meta.design_voice: Quiet, editorial, mountain-publication. Dark background like a winter sky at altitude; warm accents recall the golden hour visible on the snowline; cold accents recall ice and shadow.

teaser.prompt: Cinematic wide aspect-ratio photograph of the Nepal Himalayan range at golden hour, dramatic light raking across snow-laden ridgelines and dark rocky faces, distant glaciated peaks above 8000 meters disappearing into thin atmospheric haze, deep blue sky transitioning to amber, no people visible, no text, photorealistic editorial quality, panoramic aspect
teaser.intent: Set the scale and mood before any prose. The reader should feel the range before they see a number.
teaser.treatment: Full-bleed hero. Dark gradient overlay at the bottom for the title and dek. Subtle parallax/zoom on scroll if cheap to implement, otherwise static.

des_01.label: Hook chart: 5-year expedition rebound
des_01.chart_subtype: annotated bar with overlaid success-rate line
des_01.spec: Vega-Lite. X axis: YEAR (2020-2024). Left Y: bar height = expedition count using accent_warm fill, with the 2024 bar slightly transparent and labelled 'partial year'. Right Y: line = success_rate_pct using accent_cold. Inline annotations: '12.7x rebound' on the 2022 bar, 'deadliest Everest spring' on 2023, 'permits capped' near 2024. Title none (section heading carries it).
des_01.size: full width inside story column, ~360 px tall
des_01.intent: Communicate the volume rebound and the success-rate recovery in one chart. The line on the same axis ties the 'more climbers AND higher success' paradox together.

des_02.label: Hero photograph
des_02.intent: Reinforces the mountain scale alongside the rebound chart. Reused from teaser - it is also the section's atmospheric anchor.
des_02.treatment: Pulled into edt_01 only as a constrained-width caption image with caption attribution.

des_03.label: Three peaks own half the calendar - horizontal bar
des_03.spec: Vega-Lite horizontal bar. Y axis: peak names sorted descending by expeditions. X axis: expedition count. Top three bars (Everest, Ama Dablam, Manaslu) coloured accent_warm; rest in muted. Inline labels of count next to each bar. A subtle cumulative stripe annotation showing the 49.0% top-3 share.
des_03.intent: Show the long tail. The visual asymmetry IS the finding.

des_04.label: Success rate dot plot
des_04.spec: Vega-Lite dot plot. X axis: success rate 0-100%. Y axis: peak name (12 peaks, sorted by rate). Each dot sized by sqrt(n). A vertical reference line at the overall 74.1% success rate (computed from ana_04). Top peaks (Ama Dablam, Everest) coloured accent_summit; bottom peaks (Pumori, Baruntse) coloured accent_cold to make the spread feel cold to warm.
des_04.intent: Show that there's a 65-point spread, and that even within famous 8000ers, success differs hugely.

des_05.label: Failure mix donut + comparison stat
des_05.chart_subtype: donut chart of failure reasons among 228 failed expeditions
des_05.spec: Vega-Lite arc/donut. Slices for the top 6 reasons; remaining grouped as 'Other'. Bad weather + Bad conditions slices coloured accent_cold/danger to read 'environment'; technical/skill-related slices coloured a desaturated tone. Center label: '57.9% environment'. Adjacent: a stacked stat callout 'Weather: 34.2%   Technical: 4.0%   Accident: 2.2%' to make the contrast readable in 2 seconds.
des_05.intent: The donut is the easy read; the stat callout is the punch.

des_06.label: Oxygen line - paired bar
des_06.spec: Two bars, one for 'No oxygen 56.7%' and one for 'Used oxygen 94.4%'. Both anchored on the same axis. Use accent_cold for no-oxygen, accent_summit for oxygen. The 37.7-point gap is the annotation.
des_06.intent: Single visual that defines the section. The paired bar is intentional - simpler than a chart with multiple peaks, because the section is about the binary itself.

des_07.label: Oxygen vs deaths - selection-bias callout
des_07.spec: Tiny inline two-row table: 'No oxygen: 1.5% fatal'  'Used oxygen: 7.6% fatal'. Caveat note in muted typography below: 'Confounded with peak choice - oxygen marks the 8000ers, not lethality.' Style: not a chart, a small callout block.
des_07.intent: Display the counter-intuitive number AND defuse it with the caveat in the same visual unit.

des_08.label: Eight-thousander gallery scatter
des_08.spec: Vega-Lite scatter. X axis: success_rate_pct. Y axis: death_rate_per_1000. Bubble size: people_on_mountain (log scale). Bubble color: a warm-cold gradient by height_m. Each bubble labelled with the peak name. Reference grid lines at 75% success and 5/1000 death rate to break the chart into four quadrants. Everest will sit in the high-success high-death quadrant; Cho Oyu in the high-success no-death corner; Dhaulagiri I in the low-success moderate-death corner.
des_08.intent: Single chart that summarises the entire 8000er section: success vs danger vs scale.
des_08.editorial_notes: Annapurna I sits at 86.4% success and 2.92/1000 deaths IN THIS SLICE only. Caption must include the long-run 13.42% figure from det_04 to prevent misreading.

des_09.label: Mountain photograph
des_09.intent: Visualises the crowding implied by Everest's 4,659 people-on-mountain and 7.30 deaths per 1000 in this slice. Reads as documentary not glorifying.
des_09.treatment: Constrained-width image with caption referencing the 2023 spring season context (det_03).

des_10.label: Member vs hired death share
des_10.spec: Two paired horizontal stacked bars. Top row: 'Members' (7,226 people, 36 deaths). Bottom row: 'Sherpa & hired support' (6,716 people, 17 deaths). Bars normalised to 1000 people each, with deaths shown as a red wedge at the right. Death-rate-per-1000 labelled at the wedge. A small annotation: 'Hired staff are 32.1% of all deaths.'
des_10.intent: Make the labour story numerically tangible without implying that Sherpas are the climbers' fault. Per-1000 frame is more honest than absolute counts because team sizes differ.

des_11.label: Sherpa portrait
des_11.intent: Embodied counterpart to the chart. Shot from behind, anonymous, dignified.

des_12.label: Seasonality grid
des_12.spec: Two-panel bar chart inside one block. Panel A: expeditions per season (Spring 462, Autumn 394, Winter 21, Summer 5). Panel B: success rate per season (Spring 77.1%, Autumn 72.8%, Summer 60.0%, Winter 38.1%). Winter bar in panel B coloured accent_cold to mark the brutal drop.
des_12.intent: Two-panel keeps both dimensions visible - the calendar is bimodal AND winter is brutal.

des_13.label: Top nationalities - lollipop
des_13.spec: Vertical lollipop chart, top 15 nations sorted by count. Stem in muted, dot in accent_warm. Nepal, USA, UK highlighted with a slightly larger dot. Subtle '64 distinct nationalities total' line above.
des_13.intent: Lollipop is more legible than a cramped bar chart for 15 categories.

des_14.label: Unclimbed peaks heatmap-strip
des_14.spec: Top 10 mountain ranges by unclimbed-peak count. Bars in accent_cold. Annotation: 'Median unclimbed-peak height: 6,452 m' and 'Tallest unclimbed: 8,077 m'. Optional small inset list of the 5 unclimbed peaks above 7,500 m if the data supports it (otherwise omit).
des_14.intent: Frontier still exists - the data should make that visceral.

des_15.label: Hawley's archive - closing image
des_15.intent: Close the piece on the human origin of the dataset. A still life of journalist-craft - notebook, typewriter, lamp - that ties back to det_01.
des_15.treatment: Constrained image with a closing caption referencing 'The Himalayan Database', the non-profit that maintains Hawley's records.

structural_notes: Story column max-width 760 px for prose, 920 px for charts. Hero is full-bleed.
Use system serif for prose headings, system sans for body, monospace for numbers in stat callouts.
Charts inherit the dark theme; gridlines low-contrast (#2a2f36).
Section dividers: a thin 1 px rule in muted color, not big horizontal images, to keep editorial cadence.
Sticky table-of-contents in the right margin (desktop only) listing edt_01..edt_11 by their short titles.
